title: PHD2 cannot be configured during onboarding unless PHD2 is already running
reasoning: The claimed code is present and is a real cause fix, not a disclosure. packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/onboarding/steps/guider_step.dart now has _savePhd2Selection() which is probe-independent: it writes the draft guider ('phd2:host:port' + display name) AND persists phd2Host/phd2Port through appSettingsProvider. _useThisPhd2 (the 'Use PHD2' button, line 306-312) and _clearPhd2Selection ('Clear', 315-320) are both wired. The selection line is derived from the draft via _phd2EndpointOf(draft.guiderId), not a local bool, so a native-guider pick in the picker below (onSelected -> notifier.setGuider) retires it, exactly as claimed. The success probe path still one-taps (line 167). Traced the whole chain rather than trusting the summary: onboarding_provider.dart:407 copies draft.guiderId/guiderName into the created EquipmentProfileModel; summary_step.dart:137 renders draft.guiderName instead of the '- not set -' fallback; device_service/connections.dart:648-690 (_connectGuider) recognises the 'phd2:' id form via isPhd2DeviceId and reads settings.phd2Host/phd2Port - so persisting those two settings is load-bearing, not decorative. Checked for INVERTED: onboarding_screen.dart:216-227 still confirms before Skip drops a configured guider, so the newly always-available selection cannot be silently discarded.
evidence: Severed the production wiring: replaced the body of _useThisPhd2 with an early return when host/port parse. Both tests in test/screens/onboarding/onboarding_guider_offline_select_test.dart went red (Expected: 'phd2:192.168.1.50:4400' / Actual: <null>; Expected: not null / Actual: <null>). Restored the line and both tests plus onboarding_guider_endpoint_test.dart pass (4 green). One severed run was polluted by a concurrent agent's compile error in skotiq_planetarium (mosaic_targets.dart:252 'hoursAboveMinAlt'); re-ran once it cleared. Cosmetic edge, not a defect: a zero-padded port ('04400') makes _currentEndpoint never string-match the saved endpoint, so the button stays 'Use PHD2' with a switch-to prompt naming the same address.

title: FocusModelPanel is orphaned - the machine that builds the temperature-compensation model cannot display it
reasoning: Every factual claim checks out. `grep -rn FocusModelPanel` over packages/ and apps/ returns nothing and the file is gone (git status shows ` D packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/focus_model_panel.dart`), so the orphan claim and the deletion are both true. The replacement is really mounted: focus_panel.dart:463-472 adds a 'Temperature Compensation' heading and `const FocusModelCurveCard()` at the foot of the Focus tab, and FocusPanel is the widget imaging_screen.dart:434 puts in the tab IndexedStack - so this is the actual production Focus tab, not a sibling. The card reads focusProfileDataProvider (focus_model_curve_card.dart:114), which is backend-aware, so the 'honest on a paired companion' claim is sound, and it carries chart + quality/R2 + prediction + filter offsets as claimed. The stale comment in focus_model_settings.dart:18 now names FocusModelCurveCard and keeps the Remote-only caveat. On the dismissed second half: shell/widgets/status_bar/temperature_and_time.dart (the fixer cited the path without its `shell/` segment) is indeed a bare Tooltip -> Container -> Row with no InkWell/GestureDetector anywhere in the file, so 'clicking produced nothing' was never a broken control; the only tappable chips in that bar are web_dashboard_button.dart and session_sharing.dart, which are visibly buttons. Judgement is defensible; not inventing a defect there. Re-checked in this pass (the shard was resumed after a context death): FocusModelPanel/focus_model_panel has zero remaining code references and the file is gone; the only surviving mention is a stale waiver row at docs/production-readiness/behavioral-audit-register.md:38. Read tools/production/behavioral_audit.dart to see whether that breaks the gate - it does not: the register is only consulted as a lookup (register[filePath] / register[key]) to exempt findings, and a row matching no finding is simply unused; there is no path-existence check. So it is dead documentation, not a gate failure or a product defect. Left it alone rather than edit a shared register while other agents are in the tree. focus_panel_temp_comp_test.dart is green in the current tree.
evidence: Severed: replaced `const FocusModelCurveCard()` in focus_panel.dart with SizedBox.shrink. focus_panel_temp_comp_test.dart went red ('Found 0 widgets with type "FocusModelCurveCard"'); restored and it is green again. Checked for a layout REGRESSION the shipped test would miss - it pumps at 500dp wide, but the imaging side panel is 320dp (the same 320 that item 3 of this shard is about). Wrote a throwaway probe pumping FocusPanel at physicalSize 320x2400 with a fitted model and a connected focuser: no RenderFlex overflow, no exception, test green. Deleted the probe after use.

title: Rotator relative-move strip clips +15 deg off the card with no scroll affordance
repairSummary: In packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/imaging/widgets/rotator_panel.dart, wrapped the _RelativeMoveButton label in FittedBox(fit: BoxFit.scaleDown) with maxLines: 1 / softWrap: false and trimmed the horizontal padding 10 -> 8, so a step label scales down instead of breaking at the hyphen when the cell narrows. Rewrote packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/imaging/widgets/rotator_relative_move_fits_test.dart around a shared _pumpAt(width) helper and added two things the shipped test could not catch: (a) parameterised cases at 250 px (imaging_screen's minPanelWidth) and 220 px (adaptive_panel_layout's tablet clamp floor) asserting every label stays on one line, inside the card and hit-testable; (b) a real tap-target test that hit-tests the button box at its left and right insets against the button's own RenderPointerListener, with the inter-button gap as a negative control - the shipped test only asserted find.text(...).hitTestable(), which proves the glyphs are reachable but says nothing about the widened cell the fix's rationale rests on.
reasoning: The core of the fix is real and does address the cause: _buildRelativeMoveSection (rotator_panel.dart:470-497) is now two Rows of three Expanded cells with no SingleChildScrollView anywhere, and the label is centred (alignment: Alignment.center). Measured it rather than trusting it - at 320 px all six steps sit inside the card, and I confirmed the widened cell really is a bigger tap target (hit-testing the box 3 px from its left and right edges reaches the button's own RenderPointerListener; a point in the 8 px gap does not). But the fixer's claim is 'every step is drawn inside the card and hit-testable AT ANY PANEL WIDTH' and 'the buttons get wider rather than narrower', and that only held at the one width they measured. Removing the scroll view made the cells flexible, and the layout supports much narrower panels than 320: imaging_screen.dart:256 sets minPanelWidth: 250 (the operator can drag there) and adaptive_panel_layout.dart:183/195 clamps the tablet split down to 220. Swept panel widths and found the label word-wraps at the hyphen from ~288 px down - '-15°' renders as a line reading '-' over a line reading '15°' (measured text height 36.0 px vs 18.0 px single-line at 250 and 220 px), and the button is NARROWER there (box 57.3 px) than the intrinsic-width button it replaced. So the unreachable-control defect is genuinely gone, but a new visual defect was introduced at the narrow end of the same range - the classic partial fix, correct on the path tested. Not an overflow: no RenderFlex exception at any width down to 200, so no automated gate would have caught it.
evidence: Width sweep with a throwaway probe pumping RotatorPanel in a SizedBox at 320/300/296/292/288/280/270/260/250/240/220/200 px, printing the '-15°' text rect: single line (h=18.0) at 288 and above, two lines (h=36.0) from 280 down to 220, three lines (h=72.0) at 200; no exception at any width. After the repair the same sweep is single-line everywhere (h=18.0 at 320..288, 17.3 at 270, 14.8 at 250 - scaled, not wrapped). Reversion check: restored the plain Text and 10 px padding and the two new width cases failed with 'Expected: a value less than <24> / Actual: <36.0> ... -15° wrapped onto a second line at 250.0 px'; put the repair back and all 11 tests in rotator_relative_move_fits_test.dart + rotator_panel_angle_range_test.dart pass. Scratch probes deleted.

title: Night Narrator ticker produced zero insights across a 65-minute session with 12 frames, an autofocus run and a cooldown
reasoning: The widget half of the claim is real and correct: narrator_ticker.dart:52-54 now picks recentNarratorFeedProvider when sessionStateProvider.dbSessionId is null, _NarratorFeedSheet (line 349-351) reads the same source so strip and sheet cannot contradict each other, and _buildRotation line 142 makes the 10-minute window mandatory in the sessionless case. But the fixer's load-bearing premise is materially false. The summary asserts NarratorService 'binds guiding, weather, autofocus and last-image-stats and persists events with a null session_id', i.e. that the sessionless bucket is being filled for a hand-driven night. It is not, for the inputs this finding is about. narrator_service.dart:173 returns out of _bindStreams as soon as _sessionId == null, BEFORE the sessionImagesStreamProvider(sessionId) subscription at line 224 - and _onImagesChanged (line ~366) is the ONLY producer of _imageStats, _skySamples, _gradeEvents and _solveHistory. The imperative ingestImageStats / ingestSkySample / ingestGradeEvent / ingestSolveOutcome hooks are labelled in the source itself as 'Push hooks (test-only seams) ... These imperative seams have no production callers', and `grep -rn` over packages/ and apps/ excluding tests confirms zero callers. _bindLastImageStats does fire sessionless but only writes _pendingFwhm (line 337), which is read at exactly one place - line 389, inside _onImagesChanged - so sessionless it is a write-only dead variable. _onStageResult is bound at line 237, also inside the session-only block. And _buildContext (line 567-580) hard-codes calibrations / transparency / frameQuality / movingObjects / lightCurve / filterIntegration / diagnostics to const [] / null whenever sessionId is null. Net: on the exact scenario in the finding - 12 manual frames, an autofocus run, a cooldown - the sessionless context carries only _weather, _autofocusHfrBaseline, _guideRmsHistory, _periodResults and pushed transient candidates. Of the 22 detectors in buildDefaultNarratorEngine, that leaves GuidingDegradedDetector (needs a connected guider AND degraded guiding), PeriodFoundDetector (needs the user to run a period analysis) and the three First Light transient detectors (need plate-solved frames with a difference-imaging hit) able to speak at all. Nothing announces a cooldown at all - there is no cooling detector in the catalog. FocusDriftDetector reads ctx.imageStats (equipment_detectors.dart:168) so it is silent; every quality/milestone/conditions detector reads imageStats, skySamples, gradeEvents, solveHistory or a session-scoped field, so all are silent; the only reader of ctx.weather is CloudsVsFocusDetector (conditions_detectors.dart:276), which also needs skySamples. So the operator on a hand-driven night still sees an empty strip - the ticker now reads the correct bucket, but nothing writes to that bucket for manual frames. The defect was moved one layer down, not removed. Second, smaller problem in the same chain: sessionless dedupe is permanent. NarratorEventsDao.hasDedupeKey(null, key) and dedupeKeysForSession(null) filter on `sessionId IS NULL` with no time component, so a static-key detector - 'conditions.excellent', 'conditions.sky_darkness.darker', 'milestone.calibration_locked', 'milestone.limiting_mag.first' - can fire exactly once per install in the sessionless bucket, and never again on any later night. Session-scoped events are immune (each night gets a fresh session id); the sessionless bucket the ticker was just pointed at is not. Not a DISCLOSURE-ONLY or INVERTED fix, and nothing regressed - it is the classic INCOMPLETE shape: one link of the chain fixed, the link it depends on left broken, and the summary describing the broken link as working.
evidence: Baseline: 9/9 green in packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/imaging/widgets/narrator_ticker_test.dart. Severed the production wiring - replaced the sessionId==null ternary in NarratorTicker.build with the old `if (sessionId == null) return const SizedBox.shrink();` - and 2 tests went red ('speaks the sessionless feed when there is no DB session': Found 0 widgets with text 'Cooling reached -10.0 C'; 'sessionless headline retires once it ages out of the window': Found 0 widgets with text 'Guiding settled at 0.6"'). Restored, 9/9 green again. Note the third sessionless test, 'sessionless strip stays quiet on a stale bucket', PASSES while severed - it asserts Size.zero, which is trivially true when the widget is hidden for the wrong reason, so it pins nothing. The gap proof is structural and read directly from source, no hardware needed: narrator_service.dart:173 (early return), :224 (sessionImagesStreamProvider bind, session-only), :337 vs :389 (_pendingFwhm written sessionless, read only inside _onImagesChanged), :455-460 (the 'no production callers' comment on the push hooks), :567-580 (session-gated context fields); `grep -rn 'ingestImageStats|ingestGradeEvent|ingestSolveOutcome|ingestSkySample' packages apps` minus tests returns nothing. narrator_events_dao.dart:26-52 shows the time-free sessionless dedupe. Did not edit skotiq_core - see blockedOnSharedCode.
